summary.text: Natural rubber consists mainly of polymers of the organic compound isoprene, and the types used are classified as elastomers.
It is harvested mainly as latex from the Pará rubber tree, drawn off by cutting the bark in a process called tapping.
In most of its useful forms it has a large stretch ratio and high resilience, and it is buoyant and water-proof.

facts.label: Main source
facts.value: The Pará rubber tree, Hevea brasiliensis

facts.label: Harvest method
facts.value: Tapping: cutting the bark and collecting the latex

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: Priestley noticed in 1770 it rubbed off pencil marks

items.prompt: How do workers get latex from a rubber tree?

options.label: They crush the leaves and boil the juice
They cut incisions in the bark and collect the fluid in vessels
They cut the tree down and press the trunk
They drill deep into the roots for sap

items.explain: The latex is drawn off by making incisions in the bark and collecting the fluid in vessels, a process called tapping.

items.prompt: Many plants make latex. Why is the Pará rubber tree the main commercial source?

options.label: It grows well under cultivation and gives usable latex easily
It is the only plant that makes latex at all
It grows only in cold climates far from the tropics
Its latex has no isoprene polymers to refine out

items.explain: This species is preferred because it grows well under cultivation, and many other plants do not produce usable polymer as easily.

items.prompt: Dandelion milk contains latex of the same quality as tree rubber. Why were wild dandelions not used as a rubber crop?

options.label: Their latex is a different kind of polymer
Their latex cannot be tapped by cutting
Their latex content is low and varies greatly
Their latex dissolves in turpentine

items.explain: In the wild types of dandelion, latex content is low and varies greatly, so research on them failed until a cultivar was developed.

items.prompt: Rubber trees are native to Brazil, yet plantations later spread to Asia. How did that happen?

options.label: Brazil sold young trees to Asia through open trade laws
Seeds floated across the sea and took root on their own
Asian farmers bred rubber from local dandelions
Seeds were taken from Brazil to England, then seedlings were sent to Asian colonies

items.explain: Henry Wickham took seeds from Brazil to Kew Gardens, and seedlings were sent to India, British Ceylon, the Dutch East Indies, Singapore and British Malaya.

items.prompt: What pushed chemists toward making rubber synthetically?

options.label: Demand for rubber-like materials began to outstrip natural supplies
Natural rubber stopped being water-proof
Natural rubber was found to contain no isoprene
Natural rubber trees stopped producing latex

items.explain: Industrial demand for rubber-like materials began to outstrip natural rubber supplies by the end of the 19th century, leading to synthetic rubber in 1909.

items.prompt: How did Charles Macintosh's patent make waterproof rubberized fabric?

options.label: By soaking one cloth in latex sap until it was stiff
By weaving rubber threads through the cloth
By cementing two thicknesses of cloth together with natural rubber
By dissolving the cloth in naphtha and rubber

items.explain: The essence of his patent was cementing two thicknesses of cloth together with natural rubber.
